content:
Looking at the folds: the octagon is folded along a vertical axis, then a horizontal axis, then a diagonal axis, producing a small triangle that is 1/8 of the octagon, with the center of the octagon at one corner.

The cut removes the corner corresponding to the **center** of the octagon, with a straight cut perpendicular to one of the fold-edge sides (a radius of the octagon).

Unfolding: each of the 8 layers carries a copy of this small right-triangular notch. Reflecting the notch across the vertical, horizontal, and diagonal fold lines, the eight copies join edge-to-edge around the center. Since the cut is perpendicular to a radius (fold line along an axis), the four reflected pairs of notches combine into a single square hole whose sides are horizontal and vertical (parallel/perpendicular to the fold axes).

- A tilted square (A) would require an oblique cut.
- An octagonal hole (B, E) would require the cut perpendicular to the octagon's edge side.
- A star (D) would require cuts into the middle of sides.
- The perpendicular cut to the radius side gives an axis-aligned square hole.

\boxed{C}
